text: Consider the efficiency of Carnot's engine is given by $η=\frac{αβ}{\sin θ}\log _{e}\frac{βx}{kT}$, where $α$ and $β$ are constants. If T is temperature, k is Boltzmann constant, $θ$ is angular displacement and x has the dimensions of length. Then, choose the incorrect option :
options: Dimensions of $β$ is same as that of force.
Dimensions of $α^{-1}x$ is same as that of energy.
Dimensions of $η^{-1}\sin θ$ is same as that of $αβ$.
Dimensions of $α$ is same as that of $β$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Since, dimensions trigonometric function and logarithmic function are dimensionless quantities.

$\therefore [η]=\left [\mathrm{M}^{0}\mathrm{L}^{0}\mathrm{T}^{0}\right ]$

Also, dimensions of temperature, $[T]=\left [\mathrm{M}^{0}\mathrm{L}^{0}\mathrm{T}{}^{0}\mathrm{K}\right ]$

Dimensions of Boltzmann constant, $[k]=\left [\mathrm{ML}^{2}\mathrm{T}^{-2}\mathrm{K}^{-1}\right ]$

Dimension of $x=\left [\mathrm{M}^{0}\mathrm{LT}^{0}\right ]$

(A) $[β]=\left [\frac{kT}{x}\right ]=\left [\frac{E}{x}\right ]=[MLT^{-2}]=[F]$

(B) $[αβ]=[M^{0}L^{0}T^{0}]$

$[α]^{-1}=[β]=\left [\frac{kT}{x}\right ]$

So $[α]^{-1}[x]=[kT]=[ML^{2}T^{-2}]$

(C) $η\sin θ=αβ$

So $[η\sin θ]=[αβ]$

$[η]=[M^{0}L^{0}T^{0}]$ it is dimensionless quantity

(D) $[α]\neq [β]$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Evening Shift

text:
Consider a cylindrical tank of radius $1\mathrm{m}$ is filled with water. The top surface of water is at $15\mathrm{m}$ from the bottom of the cylinder. There is a hole on the wall of cylinder at a height of $5\mathrm{m}$ from the bottom. A force of $5\times 10^{5}\mathrm{N}$ is applied on the top surface of water using a piston. The speed of efflux from the hole will be : (given atmospheric pressure $\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{A}}=1.01\times 10^{5}\mathrm{Pa}$, density of water $ρ_{\mathrm{W}}=1000\mathrm{kg}/\mathrm{m}^{3}$ and gravitational acceleration $\mathrm{g}=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$ )


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The piston pushes on the water surface with $F=5\times 10^{5}\text{N}$ over the area $A=π(1)^{2}=π\text{m}^{2}$; the atmosphere acts on the piston, not on the water, so the pressure at the top surface of the water is

$P_{1}=\dfrac{F}{A}=\dfrac{5\times 10^{5}}{π}\text{Pa}\approx 1.59\times 10^{5}\text{Pa}$

The hole is $h=15-5=10\text{m}$ below the top surface, the jet leaves at atmospheric pressure $P_{A}$, and the speed of the top surface is negligible.

Bernoulli's equation between the top surface and the hole gives

$P_{1}+ρgh=P_{A}+\dfrac{1}{2}ρv^{2}$

$v^{2}=\dfrac{2}{ρ}(P_{1}+ρgh-P_{A})=\dfrac{2}{1000}\left (1.59\times 10^{5}+1.0\times 10^{5}-1.01\times 10^{5}\right )\approx 316\text{m}^{2}\text{s}^{-2}$

$v\approx 17.8\text{m s}^{-1}$

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Evening Shift

text:
A vessel contains $14\mathrm{g}$ of nitrogen gas at a temperature of $27^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$. The amount of heat to be transferred to the gas to double the r.m.s speed of its molecules will be :

Take $\mathrm{R}=8.32\mathrm{J}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}\mathrm{k}^{-1}$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$n=\dfrac{14}{28}=0.5\text{mol}$ and $T_{1}=27+273=300\text{K}$.

$v_{rms}=\sqrt{\dfrac{3RT}{M}}\propto \sqrt{T}$, so doubling $v_{rms}$ needs $T_{2}=4T_{1}=1200\text{K}$, i.e. $\Delta T=900\text{K}$.

The gas is held in a closed vessel, so its volume stays constant and the heat supplied equals the rise in internal energy, $Q=nC_{V}\Delta T$, with $C_{V}=\dfrac{5}{2}R$ for diatomic $\mathrm{N}{}_{2}$:

$Q=0.5\times \dfrac{5}{2}\times 8.32\times 900=9360\text{J}$

Using $C_{p}$ would give $13104\text{J}$, which applies only if the gas were allowed to expand at constant pressure.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Evening Shift

text: The distance of centre of mass from end A of a one dimensional rod (AB) having mass density $ρ=ρ_{0}\left (1-\frac{x^{2}}{L^{2}}\right )\mathrm{kg}/\mathrm{m}$ and length L (in meter) is $\frac{3L}{α}\mathrm{m}$. The value of $α$ is $___________. ($where x is the distance from end A)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For a rod of linear mass density $ρ(x)$, the centre of mass measured from end A is

$x_{cm}=\dfrac{\int\limits _{0}^{L}ρxdx}{\int\limits _{0}^{L}ρdx}$

Numerator: $ρ_{0}\int\limits _{0}^{L}\left (x-\dfrac{x^{3}}{L^{2}}\right )dx=ρ_{0}\left (\dfrac{L^{2}}{2}-\dfrac{L^{2}}{4}\right )=\dfrac{ρ_{0}L^{2}}{4}$

Denominator (total mass): $ρ_{0}\int\limits _{0}^{L}\left (1-\dfrac{x^{2}}{L^{2}}\right )dx=ρ_{0}\left (L-\dfrac{L}{3}\right )=\dfrac{2ρ_{0}L}{3}$

$x_{cm}=\dfrac{ρ_{0}L^{2}/4}{2ρ_{0}L/3}=\dfrac{3L}{8}$

Comparing with $\dfrac{3L}{α}$ gives $α=8$.

Hence, the answer is 8.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Evening Shift

text: At a certain temperature, the degrees of freedom per molecule for gas is 8. The gas performs 150 J of work when it expands under constant pressure. The amount of heat absorbed by the gas will be $_________ J$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
At constant pressure, the work done by the gas is

$W=P\Delta V=nR\Delta T=150\text{J}$

With $f=8$ degrees of freedom per molecule,

$\Delta U=\dfrac{f}{2}nR\Delta T=4\times 150=600\text{J}$

By the first law of thermodynamics,

$Q=\Delta U+W=600+150=750\text{J}$

Hence, the answer is 750.

text: An electrical bulb rated 220 V, 100 W, is connected in series with another bulb rated 220 V, 60 W. If the voltage across combination is 220 V, the power consumed by the 100 W bulb will be about $_______ W$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
From the ratings, $R=\dfrac{V^{2}}{P}$ with $V=220\text{V}$: $R_{100}=\dfrac{V^{2}}{100}=484\Omega$ and $R_{60}=\dfrac{V^{2}}{60}\approx 806.7\Omega$.

In series across $V=220\text{V}$ the current is $I=\dfrac{V}{R_{100}+R_{60}}$, so the power in the 100 W bulb is

$P_{100}^{'}=I^{2}R_{100}=\dfrac{V^{2}R_{100}}{(R_{100}+R_{60})^{2}}$

Substituting $R=\dfrac{V^{2}}{P}$, the factor $V^{4}$ cancels:

$P_{100}^{'}=\dfrac{\frac{1}{100}}{\left (\frac{1}{100}+\frac{1}{60}\right )^{2}}=\dfrac{\frac{1}{100}}{\left (\frac{4}{150}\right )^{2}}=\dfrac{22500}{1600}\approx 14.06\text{W}$

The 60 W bulb, having the larger resistance, takes the larger share, $\dfrac{22500}{960}\approx 23.4\text{W}$.

Hence, the answer is 14.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Evening Shift

text: In an experiment to find acceleration due to gravity (g) using simple pendulum, time period of $0.5\mathrm{s}$ is measured from time of 100 oscillation with a watch of $1\mathrm{s}$ resolution. If measured value of length is $10\mathrm{cm}$ known to $1\mathrm{mm}$ accuracy, The accuracy in the determination of $\mathrm{g}$ is found to be $x%$. The value of $x$ is $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For a simple pendulum, $T=2π\sqrt{\dfrac{l}{g}}$, so $g=\dfrac{4π^{2}l}{T^{2}}$ and

$\dfrac{\Delta g}{g}=\dfrac{\Delta l}{l}+2\dfrac{\Delta T}{T}$

The time of 100 oscillations is $100\times 0.5=50\text{s}$, read on a watch of resolution $1\text{s}$. Dividing by 100 does not change the fractional error, so

$\dfrac{\Delta T}{T}=\dfrac{1}{50}$

The length is $10\text{cm}=100\text{mm}$ with $\Delta l=1\text{mm}$, so $\dfrac{\Delta l}{l}=\dfrac{1}{100}$.

$\dfrac{\Delta g}{g}\times 100=\left (\dfrac{1}{100}+2\times \dfrac{1}{50}\right )\times 100=1%+4%=5%$

Hence, the answer is 5.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Evening Shift
